summary: Collects issues found in the SCTP specification during several interoperability events and years of implementation experience, with suggested fixes as changes to RFC 2960. It is informational. It was replaced by RFC 9260.

eli5.summary: A list of typos and mix-ups found in the instruction booklet after people built things with it, plus corrections. A newer booklet replaced it.

subtitle: Corrections and clarifications to the SCTP specification after five years of implementation experience.

tldr.problem: After years of real-world SCTP implementation and six interoperability testing events, numerous errors and ambiguities were discovered in RFC 2960, ranging from typos to subtle issues in congestion control, error handling, and security.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC documents all known issues found in RFC 2960 and provides the corrected text that should be used in implementations and future standards, organized chronologically in 52 errata entries with problem descriptions and solutions.
tldr.outcome: Implementers now have authoritative guidance on the correct behavior of SCTP, which improves interoperability and corrects protocol flaws. The errata were later compiled into RFC 9260, which is the current authoritative SCTP specification.

today: RFC 4460 is an Informational RFC that documented all known errata in RFC 2960. These errata were later consolidated into RFC 9260 (June 2022), which is the current authoritative specification for SCTP. The corrections ensure that implementations can properly interoperate with each other and address both specification ambiguities and security issues.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: RFC 2960 originally defined the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP), a reliable message-oriented transport layer protocol. After five years of implementation experience and six interoperability events, this document compiles all known defects found in the original specification. These defects include editorial errors, ambiguous wording, technical issues, and security problems. The document provides the problem description, the original incorrect text from RFC 2960, the replacement text, and a solution description for each error, organized chronologically as they were discovered.
sections.eli5: SCTP is a way computers talk to each other. The original instructions had mistakes. This document lists every mistake found and what it should have said.

sections.title: Structural and Formatting Issues
sections.content: Several errors involved the structure of SCTP messages and how they should be processed. For example, RFC 2960 incorrectly stated that unrecognized chunks should report a 'parameter' error when they should report a 'chunk' error. Padding of message chunks was unclear—the specification did not properly explain that the final parameter's padding should not be included in the chunk length field. Parameters needed to be unique across all chunk types, but this was not explicitly stated. Stream processing had to clarify that an INIT ACK cannot request more streams than the INIT offered. These structural clarifications prevent implementations from misinterpreting message formats.
sections.eli5: SCTP messages have different parts. The original instruction had errors about how to put those parts together and recognize mistakes. These fixes explain exactly what should be included and not included.

sections.title: Congestion Control and Data Transmission Issues
sections.content: Several critical issues involved congestion control, which prevents SCTP from overwhelming the network. The original specification was unclear about whether senders could exceed the congestion window (cwnd) even slightly, which some implementations could not work correctly with. Fast Retransmit procedures required clarification: the specification did not require senders to report gap acknowledgments (needed for detecting losses), did not limit how many times a packet could be fast retransmitted, and lacked a proper Fast Recovery procedure. The partial_bytes_acked counter needed to be reset during congestion control adjustments but this was not stated. Window probes for handling zero-window situations were not defined. The initial value of the cumulative TSN acknowledgment field needed clarification. Heartbeat and failure detection procedures were vague about when to send heartbeats, when to respond, and how to count heartbeat failures. These issues are critical because incorrect congestion control can cause network problems or poor application performance.
sections.eli5: Computers need to send data slowly enough that they do not break the network. SCTP has rules for this. The rules were confusing, so people implemented them differently. These fixes explain exactly what to do.

sections.title: Security and Error Handling
sections.content: Several security and error handling issues were critical. A major security problem: an attacker could send an INIT message to an existing association and cause a restart with new addresses, potentially hijacking the connection. The specification did not check for this. A new error code was added to report when an INIT tries to add unexpected new addresses. Address verification in COOKIE-ECHO had issues. Handling of unrecognized parameters and chunks needed clarification—the original text was ambiguous about which level (packet or chunk) should be affected by unknown parameters. The specification did not clearly state what to do with non-unicast addresses or how to handle ABORT chunks correctly. Port number 0 was not restricted properly. The Tie-Tags mechanism for distinguishing restart from collision cases needed clarification. Parameter processing and error reporting were ambiguous about when to send errors in ERROR chunks versus INIT ACK chunks.
sections.eli5: When things go wrong, computers need to send error messages that say exactly what went wrong. The original instructions were unclear about how to report errors, and there was a security hole where someone could trick a computer into starting a new connection with the wrong computer.

sections.title: Additional Clarifications
sections.content: The specification required many other clarifications: SACK (Selective Acknowledgment) packet format details, proper handling of retransmissions including Karn's Algorithm application, ICMP handling procedures, checksum computation, stream sequence number initialization, and cookie echo procedures. The specification also needed to clarify how Path MTU (Maximum Transmission Unit) discovery interacts with SCTP fragmentation, how the T3-rtx retransmission timer should behave, and what happens when there are more errors than can fit in a single error chunk. Each of these issues, while individually small, could cause interoperability failures or incorrect behavior in edge cases. Some issues required changing how implementations track data in flight, how they respond to network errors, or how they initialize connection state.
sections.eli5: The instruction manual had lots of small unclear parts. Each one could cause two different computers to work differently. These fixes explain each part clearly so they will work together.
